title: Direkte salg av potet og grønnsaker i Troms og Finnmark. Resultater fra en intervjuundersøkelse blant småskala grøntprodusenter (NIBIO Rapport 9(79) 2023) — presentasjon

findings.claim: Intervjuundersøkelse blant 11 småskala grøntprodusenter (9 Troms, 2 Finnmark) og 4 representanter for salgskanaler (Bondens marked, REKO, dagligvare, digital plattform)

Salgskanaler brukt av småskala grøntprodusenter: ubetjent/betjent gårdsutsalg, REKO-ring, Bondens Marked, digital plattform, levering til privatkunder, direkte til restaurant/storkjøkken og direkte til dagligvarebutikk

Rapporterte utfordringer: klima, mangel på produsentnettverk, lange avstander/små markeder, tidspress, lav lønnsomhet, manglende infrastruktur, innpass i dagligvare, lite offentlig støtte, regelverk for skilting

limitations: Staget kopi er presentasjons-/foredragsversjonen (Statsforvalteren-hostet), ikke full rapporttekst; kvalitativ intervjustudie, n=11, ikke representativt utvalg.

title: NorgesGruppen ASA — Credit Research, 25 November 2015

findings.claim: NorgesGruppen owns more than 800,000 sqm of real estate across more than 200 properties, predominantly retail stores, plus warehouses
NorgesGruppen holds a 49% stake in Scala Retail Property (51% Fredriksborg AS); sale of Grorud/Rykkin/Tangen Nærsenter and Fagernes Shopping Centre to Scala completed 1 May 2015
NorgesGruppen grocery market share 39.9% in 2014 (+0.5pp from 2013, AC Nielsen); the three players NG, Coop SA and ReitanGruppen together held 96.4% of the market

Private labels comprise at least 13–14% of total grocery turnover, rising to ~30% in categories like fresh meat and produce (grocery sales ~160 bn NOK/yr)

limitations: Opinion/interview article (expert commentary), not primary data. Figures attributed to Prof. Hem.

Direct-to-consumer channels for local food: farmers' markets, farm shops, internet sales, REKO rings (social-media-based direct sales), gourmet food stores; micro-businesses build new categories in the grocery market (Paper 3: 4 pioneering cases)

title: Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010

findings.claim: The Order requires designated large grocery retailers to release restrictive covenants that restrict grocery retailing (Art.4(1)) and bars new such covenants (Art.5(1)); existing exclusivity arrangements must stop being enforced within 5 years (Art.7(1)), new ones capped at 5 years (Art.8)

Geographic competition test (Schedule 4): 10-minute drive-time isochrone; where a retailer controls multiple stores with >=60% market share in a concentrated local market (<=3 competing fascias), covenants/exclusivity fail and must be released
Designated Large Grocery Retailers (Schedule 1): Asda, Co-operative Group, Marks & Spencer, Morrisons, Sainsbury's, Tesco, Waitrose (plus agents/subsidiaries)

limitations: Legal instrument (remedy from Competition Commission's 2008 groceries investigation); UK comparator for the Norwegian negative-servitutt ban.
